recommendation_summary: Recommends building one small local script now that reads the client's code list, matches it to JPEGs by code prefix plus separator, writes numbered copies and a contact-sheet PDF in the supplied order, and stops if any code or image doesn't match. It adds nothing optional. It asks for a sample code list, the job's filenames, and how to order multiple shots of one code.

labels.Requirements and who asked: images delivered in the client's supplied code order (client); remove the hour of manual dragging per delivery (you); a contact-sheet PDF per job (your current deliverable).
labels.Deleted: DAM, AI tagging, semantic search, cloud review portal. Nothing in your problem needs them, since the client already gives you exact codes and every filename already starts with one.
labels.Bottleneck: hand-ordering thumbnails, which a computer can do exactly from the code list.
labels.Checked myself: only what you told me. Exact ordered codes per job, filenames prefixed with the code, final JPEGs in one folder per job, an hour lost each delivery.

note: A bounded local script follows the client's order, the full stack is explicitly deleted, and the checks are limited to the facts the user supplied.
